self_description_brief: PhD Candidate in Computer Science building LLM, NLP, and ML systems for AI engineering roles
self_description_detail: Hello! I am Kshitiz Tiwari, a PhD Candidate in Computer Science at the University of Arkansas specializing in Natural Language Processing, Large Language Models, and Causal Inference. I am actively looking for AI Engineer, Machine Learning Engineer, and NLP-focused roles where I can start the next phase of my career after completing my PhD.

I am strongest at turning research ideas into working AI systems: building NLP pipelines, designing retrieval-augmented generation workflows, training and evaluating transformer models, creating semantic search and ranking systems, and writing reproducible research code that can be tested, inspected, and extended.

My research focuses on controllable, robust, and interpretable language models. I work on counterfactual text generation, causal NLP, adversarial robustness, representation learning, and methods that help language models change targeted attributes while preserving meaning.

I have published research on robust NLP systems and adversarial resilience, including work presented at AACL-IJCNLP and in the Entropy journal. I also build applied AI projects involving LLM orchestration, semantic embeddings, multimodal modeling, candidate ranking, and evidence-grounded retrieval systems.

On the engineering side, I am comfortable with Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, Sentence-BERT, FastAPI, vector search, data processing, evaluation workflows, and the practical pieces needed to move from experiments to usable tools.

I am especially interested in teams working on applied LLM systems, NLP products, information retrieval, trustworthy AI, and ML infrastructure. If you are hiring for AI Engineer, ML Engineer, NLP Engineer, or Applied Scientist roles, I would be happy to connect.
